## Key North Carolina Statutory & Insurance Facts
- Licensed in all 100 NC counties (NC Agency License #15569731, NPN #6608086)
- NC minimum auto liability limits (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-279.21, Session Law 2023-133 / SB 452): **50/100/50** ($50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $50,000 property damage) plus mandatory UM/UIM for policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025
- NC continuous liability, plate surrender & lapse rules (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-309(d), § 20-309.2 & § 20-311): Vehicle owners should surrender their NC registration plate before terminating liability insurance unless financial responsibility is maintained in another permitted manner; § 20-311 governs civil penalties ($50 / $100 / $150 based on prior assessed penalties in the preceding 3 years), registration revocation, and statutory exceptions
- NC auto insurance residency & eligible-risk verification (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 58-2-164): Insurers and agents have 25 days after binding to verify a North Carolina physical garaging address using one of nine statutory documents (utility bill for a served NC address, NC driver's license, NC vehicle registration, lease/mortgage, property tax receipt, military/student ID, or federal tax return — wireless cell phone bills do not qualify)
- NC 75% Total Loss Claims Threshold vs. Salvage Definition: Under claims settlement rule **11 NCAC 04 .0418**, an insurer must treat a vehicle as a total loss when repair costs (including supplements) equal or exceed 75% of preaccident Actual Cash Value (ACV), whereas **N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-4.01(33)(d)**, **§ 20-109.1**, and **§ 20-71.3** govern salvage definitions and title branding
- NC 2026 Personal Auto Rate Bureau Filing & Oct 1, 2026 Program Revisions: No statewide voluntary private passenger auto or motorcycle base rate level increase filed for 2026; approved Personal Auto Policy Program revisions effective October 1, 2026 update deductible options and increase basic transportation expense theft limits to $30/day ($900 max)
- NC 2026–2027 Homeowners & Dwelling Rate Settlements (NCDOI / NCRB): Statewide homeowners average base rate increased 7.5% on June 1, 2026 (following 7.5% on June 1, 2025) with a rate-freeze provision prohibiting another statewide homeowners base rate increase before June 1, 2027; separate Dwelling (DP-1/DP-3 landlord & non-owner-occupied) settlement (NCRB Circular P-26-5) sets a 5% statewide average annual increase effective October 1, 2026 and 5% effective October 1, 2027
- NC Homeowners Consent to Rate (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 58-36-30(b)): Allows insurers to charge above the manual NC Rate Bureau rate with required policy disclosures; independent agents can compare carriers that do not require a Consent to Rate surcharge on the same home

## NC Auto Tools and Official Sources

- [VIN decoder](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/auto-center/free-vin-decoder): Vehicle specifications and model-level recall information. Confirm open recalls for the exact VIN with NHTSA. VIN requirements: [49 CFR Part 565](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-V/part-565).
- [DMV and SDIP points calculator](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/auto-center/sdip-points-calculator/): Educational estimates distinguishing license points from insurance points. Sources: N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 20-16, 58-36-65 and 58-36-75; [current NCDOI SDIP guidance](https://www.ncdoi.gov/consumers/auto-and-vehicle-insurance/safe-driver-incentive-plan).
- [Plate surrender before cancellation](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/blog/blogs/why-north-carolina-makes-you-turn-in-your-tag-before-you-cancel-car-insurance): N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-309(d). Lapse penalties and applicable exceptions: § 20-311.
- [Online lapse-penalty payment instructions](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/blog/blogs/how-to-pay-an-ncdmv-insurance-lapse-fee-online-via-myncdmv-in-2026): Procedural guide. For payment and FS-1 troubleshooting, use the [insurance-lapse help hub](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/auto-center/pay-dmv-fine/). Governing statute: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-311.
- [Total-loss formula and repair-to-value calculation](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/blog/blogs/nc-total-loss-formula-2026): Claims settlement rule: 11 NCAC 04 .0418. Salvage definition: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-4.01(33)(d). See [NCDOI claims guidance](https://www.ncdoi.gov/consumers/auto-and-vehicle-insurance/after-accident).
- [Household-driver listing and regular vehicle access](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/blog/blogs/non-owners-policy-household-member-north-carolina): Educational guidance directing drivers to the household vehicle's insurer. Bill Layne Insurance Agency does not write non-owner policies.
- [New-car insurance notification](https://www.billlayneinsurance.com/blog/blogs/new-car-dealer-notify-insurance): Confirm the vehicle and requested coverages directly with the insurer. Newly acquired vehicle provisions depend on the actual policy.
